svg.title: Classical rotor energy transfer and proposed quantum continuation
svg.desc: A zero-total-angular-momentum classical ring, an exact planar-pair pendulum benchmark, and a clearly marked unrun quantum rotor proposal.
svg.text: Rotor studies: transfer, delayed release, and a quantum question
These are mechanical rotors with orientation-dependent torques, separate from the FL face-channel model.
1 · Classical 3D ring: zero total angular momentum
Initially a neighboring pair carries equal-and-opposite tangent momenta; other rotors start cold.
in the hot pair through time 2,000.
Eight rotors, packet energy 18 times one bond: transfer stays below 1% through time 2,000.
Mean transfer is 29–32% over times 200–10,000: release is delayed, not cut off.
One moving rotor, one initially at rest; aligned starts.
Equal inertias and zero momentum give equal rotor energies.
3 · Quantum continuation and parallel four-rotor study

svg.title: $\text{Quantize each orientation on }S^2;\quad E_j=\frac{\hbar^2j(j+1)}{2I},\quad j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$

svg.text: The pair benchmark needs a total-angular-momentum sector; it sets the boundary condition.
Parallel work is implementing four planar rotors at exactly zero total momentum;
no result from that calculation is shown here.
No pair result is inferred here.
